recent.summary: A Democratic congressional sweep triggered the biggest post-midterm Dow rally in 44 years (+3%), with mega-cap tech (MSFT +6.7%, AMZN +6.1%) and consumer names (MCD +6.5%) surging on election clarity and rotation into lower-risk sectors. Defense (LMT -6.9%) and energy (XOM -4.6%) cratered as Vance repudiated the Iran war and Democratic policy shifts erased geopolitical risk premiums. DDOG collapsed 14.4% on a beat-and-lower earnings reaction, reinforcing that AI/cloud remains treacherous even on strong fundamentals, while the open AMZN BUY from $245.63 extended to +8.3%.

The Nasdaq plunged 5.5% into correction territory — its worst chip selloff since Covid — fully erasing the post-election rally as AI spending fears and Democrat data center regulation concerns crushed semis (MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%, TSM -10.8%) and crypto-adjacent names (MARA -14.5%). Capital rotated hard into defensive safe-havens, with COST and SAP the only green names in a 30-stock universe. Key signals: AMD BUY cut at -16.4% loss, NVDA re-entered at oversold levels (MEDIUM confidence), PLTR SELL extended to +11.6% gain, and AMZN BUY held resilient at +6.0%.

Semiconductors and AI names staged a sharp rebound led by AMD (+11% on record revenue) and TSM (+6.3%), reversing last week's brutal chip selloff and confirming intact AI demand. Mega-cap tech (MSFT, AAPL) lagged the recovery while defense and consumer defensives continued their post-election unwind. Capital rotation is selectively back into growth — NVDA and AMZN BUYs are working, PLTR SELL is +8.6% in favor, and MSFT BUY was cut on a fresh negative catalyst (Oracle cloud deal wind-down).

A broad risk-on surge drove the Dow up 1,100+ points, with semiconductors and AI names leading — AMD soared 13.3% on a Google Cloud EPYC design win and Oppenheimer upgrade, NET jumped 9.3% on a blowout Q3 beat-and-raise, and AVGO gained 8.8% on sector momentum. NVDA was the lone major decliner (-4.3%) as a WSJ-reported CEO probe into Jensen Huang created governance and succession uncertainty, prompting a signal flip to SELL. Key lessons reinforce requiring multi-source fundamental confirmation before BUY entries and treating leadership risk as an immediate exit trigger.

A hotter-than-expected CPI print reignited Fed 50bps rate-hike fears, sending Treasury yields surging and dragging Nasdaq lower — NVDA fell 5.5% (extending the open SELL to +5.5% in favor) while MSFT dropped 2.2% as high-multiple AI/tech names bore the brunt. Defense stocks (LMT +2.5%) found a bid after the House blocked Hegseth's impeachment, restoring DoD spending visibility, and crypto-adjacent MARA surged 10.5% even as broader risk appetite deteriorated. Net/TSM showed exceptional relative strength on strong fundamentals, while COIN underperformed its crypto peers, reinforcing caution on exchange-specific names amid rate headwinds.

CoreWeave's 168% revenue beat reignited the AI infrastructure trade, driving broad semiconductor gains with MU +11.9%, ORCL +8.8%, and INTC +7.5%, while TSM and MU BUYs are well in the money. NVDA surged +2.87% intraday but collapsed ~8% after-hours on multi-source reports of a board vote to remove CEO Jensen Huang, keeping the open SELL from $178.67 firmly in profit. Mega-cap tech (MSFT, META, AMZN) lagged badly on a broadly green tape, reinforcing persistent relative weakness and active SELL signals in those names.

Jensen Huang's abrupt NVDA CEO resignation is the dominant catalyst, sending NVDA down 4.3% while AMD and AVGO surge ~5.5-5.9% on rotation into alternative semis; the open NVDA SELL from $178.67 is now +7.0% in favor. Crypto-adjacent names (MSTR -6.5%, MARA -6.0%) are cratering under rising yield pressure alongside a Microsoft outage dragging mega-cap tech, keeping broad indices in the red. Energy names (XOM +1.84%) caught a bid from a Houthi attack on a Saudi pipeline, while AVGO and GOOGL emerge as the cleanest new BUY setups amid persistent AI infrastructure demand.

weekly.summary: A BofA AI bubble warning, CoreWeave credit stress, and VIX spiking above 22 triggered a four-session, $260B+ risk-off unwind crushing high-multiple AI, cloud, and crypto names (PLTR, SNOW -8%+, MSTR -9.6% with added MSCI removal headwinds, MARA -9.6%). Capital rotated decisively into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) on Middle East escalation via Yemen missile strikes and a US SPR solicitation, while AAPL held as the lone resilient core-tech name on iPhone demand, Chinese subsidies, and Berkshire support. Core calls — **BUY RTX, LMT, AAPL; SELL PLTR, MSTR** — remained fully intact across all sessions.

**Week Summary (3 sentences):**

AI/cloud and cybersecurity (DDOG, NET, AMZN) were the dominant BUY themes, fueled by SpaceX compute demand, PHP vulnerability spikes, and Iran escalation-driven infrastructure bids — with NET and DDOG delivering strong gains — though the Nasdaq's worst session since June, triggered by chipmaking supply warnings and META AI spending fears, crushed semis (AMD -8.1%, INTC -8.0%) and pulled the broader growth complex below its 50-day MA. Defense was a major early-week driver via NOC's $110B backlog, LMT's ~7% F-35 surge, and RTX read-across BUYs, but geopolitical risk-premium fading and Ukraine peace talk resumption sparked a late-week rotation out of the sector, while capital shifted defensively into cybersecurity and energy infrastructure as Iran escalation entered day two. MSTR and PLTR SELLs were badly burned (-12.2% and -8.4%) by crypto regulatory clarity and the AI rebound, AAPL was downgraded on foldable sell-the-news risk, and AMZN BUY was closed at -5.5% and flipped to SELL ahead of earnings — leaving NET (+6.0%), DDOG (+3.6%), and LMT (+2.4%) as the week's cleanest working calls.

**Summary:** AI infrastructure euphoria rapidly reversed into a sector-wide reckoning — early BUY validation from ORCL, Azure, and Anthropic's IPO gave way to INTC's -28.6% collapse, GOOGL's worst-ever single-day drop (-12.6%) on structural search fears, and broad semi weakness (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, DDOG all deeply underwater), leaving the Nasdaq on pace for its worst month in over a year. Capital rotated decisively into Defense (LHX +6.84%, RTX, LMT outperforming on $11B missile awards and DoD spending), Energy (XOM, CVX bid up on Hormuz tanker fires and Saudi evacuation orders), and Consumer Staples (WMT), while Big Tech earnings sharply divided the tape with AMZN on WATCH amid AI capex overhang. Key active calls are BUY LHX, RTX, LLY; high-conviction SELL GOOGL and META; a hawkish Fed hold at 3.75–4.0% and tighter sell discipline on AI longs represent the principal forward risks.

**Week 1 November Summary:** Markets whipsawed between a sharp growth-to-defensive rotation early in the week—hammering AI/cloud names like ORCL (-8.8%) and INTC (-8.8%) while lifting WMT and COST 3-4%—before a broad Election Day risk-on rebound reversed many of those moves, with crypto-adjacent names (MARA +11%, Riot +14%), AI semis (AMD earnings blowout), and cloud (ORCL +5.8%) surging. AMZN remained the standout long throughout on AWS/e-commerce strength, while GOOGL and DDOG stayed in downtrends and energy faded as US-Iran deal hopes eroded geopolitical premium, pressuring the open XOM BUY. New BUYs were initiated on AMD, COIN, and AMZN, AAPL and PLTR were flagged as SELLs, and the track record remained challenged at 47%/33% win rate with the ORCL SELL hitting max loss against the sharp short-squeeze rebound.
